eng112-01.stem: The bus driver often complains about chewing gum found under passenger seats because it is ＿＿＿＿ and very hard to remove.
eng112-01.ex:
句意：公車司機常抱怨座位底下的口香糖，因為它很＿＿＿又很難清掉。

(A) sticky 黏的 ✓

(B) greasy 油膩的 (C) clumsy 笨拙的 (D) mighty 強大的。
eng112-01.k: sticky＝黏黏的，所以 very hard to remove（很難清除）。

eng112-02.stem: Jesse is a talented model. He can easily adopt an elegant ＿＿＿＿ for a camera shoot.
eng112-02.ex:
句意：Jesse 是很有天分的模特兒，拍照時能輕鬆擺出優雅的＿＿＿。

(C) pose 姿勢 ✓

(A) clap 拍手 (B) toss 拋擲 (D) snap 啪的一聲、快照。

eng112-03.stem: In order to draw her family tree, Mary tried to trace her ＿＿＿＿ back to their arrival in North America.
eng112-03.ex:
句意：為了畫家譜，Mary 試著把她的＿＿＿追溯到他們抵達北美洲的時候。

family tree（家譜）→ (C) ancestors 祖先 ✓

(A) siblings 兄弟姊妹 (B) commuters 通勤者 (D) instructors 講師。
eng112-03.k: trace one's ancestors back to…＝追溯祖先到…。

eng112-04.stem: Upon the super typhoon warning, Nancy rushed to the supermarket—only to find the shelves almost ＿＿＿＿ and the stock nearly gone.
eng112-04.ex:
句意：一聽到超級颱風警報，Nancy 衝到超市，卻發現貨架幾乎＿＿＿。

bare 空的、光禿禿的 → (B) ✓

(A) blank 空白的（紙、表格）、(C) hollow 中空的（樹幹、牆），都不是「東西被買光」的意思（各約 30% 誤選）。

(D) queer 奇怪的。
eng112-04.k: bare shelves＝貨架空空的（被搶購一空）。

eng112-05.stem: Even though Jack said “Sorry!” to me in person, I did not feel any ＿＿＿＿ in his apology.
eng112-05.ex:
句意：雖然 Jack 當面對我說了「對不起」，我在他的道歉中感受不到任何＿＿＿。

(D) sincerity 真誠 ✓

(B) generosity 慷慨（24% 誤選）(A) liability 責任、負債 (C) integrity 正直。

eng112-06.stem: My grandfather has astonishing powers of ＿＿＿＿ . He can still vividly describe his first day at school as a child.
eng112-06.ex:
句意：我祖父有驚人的＿＿＿，到現在還能生動地描述他小時候第一天上學的情形。

後句「還能生動描述小時候的事」→ 記性好 → (D) recall 記憶力 ✓（powers of recall 是常見說法）

(A) resolve 決心 (B) fraction 小部分、分數 (C) privilege 特權。
eng112-06.k: powers of recall＝記憶力（recall 當名詞是「回想、記憶」）。

eng112-07.stem: Recent research has found lots of evidence to ＿＿＿＿ the drug company’s claims about its “miracle” tablets for curing cancer.
eng112-07.ex:
句意：最近的研究找到許多證據來＿＿＿這家藥廠對它治癌「神藥」的說法。

證據是用來「反駁」藥廠的說法 → (B) counter 反駁、反擊 ✓

(C) expose 揭露（全國 33% 誤選；常用來揭露祕密、醜聞，或 expose A as B「揭穿 A 是 B」）(A) provoke 激起、挑釁 (D) convert 轉換、改變信仰。

這題四個選項的選答率幾乎一樣，counter 當動詞的用法很多人不熟。
eng112-07.k: evidence to counter the claims＝反駁說法的證據。

eng112-08.stem: Corrupt officials and misguided policies have ＿＿＿＿ the country’s economy and burdened its people with enormous foreign debts.
eng112-08.ex:
句意：貪官和錯誤的政策＿＿＿國家的經濟，還讓人民背負龐大的外債。

「貪官、錯誤政策」造成的是負面結果 → (A) crippled 使癱瘓、重創 ✓

(B) accelerated 加速（全國 31% 誤選；accelerate the economy 是「促進經濟成長」，是正面意思）(C) rendered 使成為（後面要接受詞＋補語）(D) ventured 冒險。
eng112-08.k: cripple the economy＝重創經濟（cripple＝使癱瘓）。

eng113-01.stem: People who desire a ＿＿＿＿ figure should exercise regularly and maintain healthy eating habits.
eng113-01.ex:
句意：想要＿＿＿身材的人應規律運動、維持健康飲食。

(B) slender 苗條的 ✓（正面意涵，常搭 figure）。

(C) slight 常指「輕微的」，形容身材時偏向瘦小單薄，不是一般追求的體態（全國 29% 誤選）。

(A) spicy 辣的 (D) slippery 滑的。

eng113-02.stem: Watching the sun ＿＿＿＿ from a sea of clouds is a must-do activity for all visitors to Ali Mountain.
eng113-02.ex:
句意：看太陽從雲海中＿＿＿，是阿里山遊客必做的活動。

(A) emerging 浮現、出現 ✓

(D) floating 漂浮（全國 18% 誤選）(B) flashing 閃爍 (C) rushing 衝。
eng113-02.k: the sun emerging from a sea of clouds＝太陽從雲海中升起。

eng113-03.stem: Do you know what time the next bus is ＿＿＿＿ ? I’ve been waiting here for more than 30 minutes.
eng113-03.ex:
句意：你知道下一班公車幾點＿＿＿嗎？我已經等超過 30 分鐘了。

What time is the next bus due? → (B) due 預定到達的 ✓

(C) bound 要用 be bound for＋地點「開往…」，不能單獨接時間（全國 24% 誤選）。

(A) apt 易於…的 (D) docked 停泊（船）。四個選項選擇率都在 25% 左右，due 這個用法很多人不熟。

eng113-04.stem: The roasting heat and high ＿＿＿＿ made me feel hot and sticky, no matter what I did to cool off.
eng113-04.ex:
句意：炙熱的天氣加上高＿＿＿，不管怎麼消暑都覺得又熱又黏。

(B) humidity 濕度 ✓

(D) atmosphere 大氣、氣氛（全國 21% 誤選）(A) density 密度 (C) circulation 循環。
eng113-04.k: high humidity＝濕度高，才會 hot and sticky（又熱又黏）。

eng113-05.stem: Artwork created by truly great artists such as Picasso and Monet will no doubt ＿＿＿＿ the test of time.
eng113-05.ex:
句意：畢卡索、莫內等偉大藝術家的作品，無疑能＿＿＿時間的考驗。

(D) stand ✓——stand the test of time 是固定片語。

(B) take a test 是「參加考試」，不是「經得起考驗」（全國 25% 誤選）。
eng113-05.k: stand the test of time＝經得起時間的考驗（固定片語）。

eng113-06.stem: In some countries, military service is ＿＿＿＿ for men only; women do not have to serve in the military.
eng113-06.ex:
句意：在某些國家，只有男性必須＿＿＿服兵役；女性不用。

「必須服役」→ (C) compulsory 義務的、強制的 ✓

(D) distinctive 獨特的（29% 誤選）(A) forceful 強而有力的（26% 誤選）(B) realistic 實際的。
eng113-06.k: compulsory＝強制的、義務的；後句 women do not have to serve 是對照。

eng113-07.stem: The team complained that its leader always took the ＿＿＿＿ for all the hard work done by the team members.
eng113-07.ex:
句意：團隊抱怨領導者總是把成員辛苦完成的工作＿＿＿。

take the credit for sth＝居功 → (D) credit ✓

(A) take advantage of 是「利用」，後面要接 of，不接 for（全國 39% 誤選）。

(B) revenge 報復 (C) remedy 補救。
eng113-07.k: take the credit for＝把功勞攬在自己身上。

eng113-08.stem: Located at the center of the city, the business hotel ＿＿＿＿ not only good service but also convenient public transport.
eng113-08.ex:
句意：這家商務旅館位於市中心，＿＿＿不只有好服務，還有便利的大眾運輸。

(C) promises 保證提供 ✓——描述旅館「能帶給客人什麼」。

(B) contains 包含，指容器或物體內含某物，不能說旅館 contains 交通便利（全國 58% 誤選，是本週最容易錯的陷阱）。

(A) proposes 提議 (D) confirms 確認。
eng113-08.k: promise＝保證會有（某種好處）；contain 是「實體裡面裝著」。

eng113-09.stem: As blood supplies have fallen to a critically low level, many hospitals are making an ＿＿＿＿ for the public to donate blood.
eng113-09.ex:
句意：血庫存量降到危險的低點，許多醫院正＿＿＿民眾捐血。

make an appeal for sb to do sth → (A) appeal 呼籲 ✓

(C) operation 手術（26% 誤選）(B) approach 方法 (D) observation 觀察。
eng113-09.k: make an appeal for the public to…＝呼籲大眾去做…。

eng113-10.stem: David felt disappointed when he found out that he could not choose his study partners, but would be ＿＿＿＿ placed in a study group.
eng113-10.ex:
句意：David 發現不能自己選讀書夥伴，而是會被＿＿＿分組，覺得很失望。

不能自己選 → (B) randomly 隨機地 ✓

(A) eligibly 合格地 (C) apparently 顯然 (D) consequently 因此。

eng114-01.stem: If you put a ＿＿＿＿ under a leaking faucet, you will be surprised at the amount of water collected in 24 hours.
eng114-01.ex:
句意：如果你在漏水的水龍頭下放一個＿＿＿，你會很驚訝 24 小時能接到多少水。

要「接水」→ (C) container 容器 ✓

(A) border 邊界 (B) timer 計時器 (D) marker 麥克筆、標記。
eng114-01.k: put a container under a leaking faucet＝在漏水的水龍頭下放容器接水。

eng114-02.stem: The local farmers’ market is popular as it offers a variety of fresh seasonal ＿＿＿＿ to people in the community.
eng114-02.ex:
句意：當地的農夫市集很受歡迎，因為它提供社區民眾各種新鮮的當季＿＿＿。

(A) produce 農產品 ✓——fresh seasonal produce 新鮮當季農產品。

produce 當名詞時重音在第一音節（PRO-duce），當動詞時在第二音節。

(B) fashion 時尚 (C) brand 品牌 (D) trend 趨勢。

eng114-03.stem: As the years have passed by, many of my childhood memories are already ＿＿＿＿ ; I can no longer recall clearly what happened back then.
eng114-03.ex:
句意：隨著歲月流逝，我許多童年記憶已經＿＿＿；我再也記不清楚…。

後句「記不清楚」→ (A) blurring 變模糊 ✓

(C) draining 流失、耗盡（全國 24% 誤選），多用於金錢、體力，不用來形容記憶模糊。

(B) trimming 修剪 (D) glaring 刺眼的。
eng114-03.k: memories are blurring＝記憶變得模糊。

eng114-04.stem: Racist remarks are by nature ＿＿＿＿ and hurtful, and should be avoided on all occasions.
eng114-04.ex:
句意：種族歧視的言論本質上就是＿＿＿又傷人的，任何場合都應避免。

(C) offensive 冒犯的 ✓

(B) furious 狂怒的（形容人的情緒，全國 23% 誤選）(A) excessive 過度的 (D) stubborn 固執的。
eng114-04.k: offensive＝冒犯的、令人不舒服的；與 hurtful（傷人的）並列。

eng114-05.stem: Not satisfied with the first ＿＿＿＿ of her essay, Mary revised it several times before turning it in to the teacher.
eng114-05.ex:
句意：Mary 對作文的第一份＿＿＿不滿意，交給老師前改了好幾次。

(C) draft 草稿 ✓

(A) text 文本、簡訊 (B) brush 刷子 (D) plot 情節（全國 20% 誤選）。
eng114-05.k: first draft＝初稿；revised it several times＝改了好幾次。

eng114-06.stem: Left ＿＿＿＿ for years, the deserted house was filled with a thick coating of dust and a smell of old damp wood.
eng114-06.ex:
句意：這棟廢棄的房子＿＿＿多年，積了厚厚的灰塵，還有舊濕木頭的味道。

(D) vacant 空置的 ✓——left vacant for years。

(C) remote 偏遠的（全國 20% 誤選），與「積灰塵」沒有直接因果。

(A) casual 隨意的 (B) fragile 易碎的。
eng114-06.k: left vacant＝閒置、空著；deserted house＝廢棄的房子。

eng114-07.stem: The high school student showed ＿＿＿＿ courage when she helped the old man escape from the fire.
eng114-07.ex:
句意：那名高中生幫老人逃離火場時，展現了＿＿＿的勇氣。

(D) enormous 極大的 ✓——可形容抽象名詞（enormous courage/pressure）。

(A) gigantic 巨大的，多用於體積、形體（全國 21% 誤選）。

(B) exclusive 獨家的 (C) multiple 多重的。
eng114-07.k: enormous courage＝極大的勇氣；gigantic 多形容實體的「巨大」。

eng114-08.stem: Publicly financed projects are often ＿＿＿＿ or delayed during tough economic times due to a lack of resources.
eng114-08.ex:
句意：經濟不景氣時，公家出資的工程常因資源不足而被＿＿＿或延後。

與 delayed 並列、原因是缺乏資源 → (A) halted 停止 ✓

(B) hatched 孵化、策劃（全國 21% 誤選）(C) possessed 擁有 (D) reinforced 加強。

eng114-09.stem: Despite his busy schedule, the President ＿＿＿＿ the school’s graduation ceremony with his presence and a heartwarming speech.
eng114-09.ex:
句意：儘管行程忙碌，總統仍＿＿＿學校的畢業典禮，並發表暖心演說。

grace A with one's presence 是固定用法：「以某人的出席為 A 增光」→ (B) graced ✓

(C) addressed 可以指「對…演說」，但不能接 with his presence（全國 43% 誤選）。

(A) praised 稱讚 (D) credited 歸功於。
eng114-09.k: grace … with one's presence＝蒞臨增光。

eng114-10.stem: The manager of the company was sued for ＿＿＿＿ abusing his colleagues, calling them “hopeless losers.”
eng114-10.ex:
句意：這位經理因為＿＿＿辱罵同事、罵他們「無可救藥的魯蛇」而被告。

罵人是用說的 → (A) verbally 言語上地 ✓

(B) dominantly 占優勢地 (C) legitimately 合法地 (D) relevantly 相關地。
eng114-10.k: verbally abuse＝言語辱罵（calling them "hopeless losers"）。

eng114-11.stem: None of them had any idea they were about to create a social innovation that 11 rapidly around the world.
eng114-11.ex:
句意：他們當時都不知道，自己即將創造一個會迅速＿＿＿到全世界的社會創新。

they were about to create（當時即將創造）→ 擴散是那之後才發生的事 → 用「過去的未來」would spread ✓

(A) had spread、(C) had been spreading 是過去完成式，表示 1995 年以前就已經擴散，時間順序顛倒。

(D) would have spread 表示「本來會擴散（但沒有）」，和事實（後來真的擴散到全世界）相反。
eng114-11.k: 從 1995 年的時間點看「之後會」擴散 → would＋原形動詞（過去的未來）。

eng114-12.stem: With their plan 12 by the rain, the two dozen participants squeezed into the living room.
eng114-12.ex:
句意：原本要在花園圍大圈討論，不巧下起大雨。計畫被雨＿＿＿，二十多位參與者只好擠進客廳。

下雨讓計畫「被打亂」→ (B) disrupted ✓

(A) facilitated 促進 (C) disclosed 揭露 (D) fulfilled 實現，都和「只好擠進客廳」矛盾。
eng114-12.k: With their plan disrupted by the rain＝計畫被雨打亂（with＋名詞＋過去分詞）。

eng114-13.stem: They periodically stopped their conversations to switch tables so the insights and ideas might 13 and deepen.
eng114-13.ex:
句意：他們定期停下來換桌，讓大家的見解與想法能夠＿＿＿並且深化。

換桌的目的是讓想法在不同桌之間「流通」→ (A) circulate 流通、傳播 ✓（下一句也說換桌時看到新想法冒出來）

(B) emphasize 強調（及物動詞，後面要接受詞）(C) recover 恢復 (D) preserve 保存，都不是換桌能達成的效果。

這題四個選項的選答率很接近，是這一組最難的一題。
eng114-13.k: ideas might circulate and deepen＝想法得以流通並深化；呼應 switch tables（換桌）。

eng114-14.stem: Over the course of the morning, the innovative discussion process 14 a new form of collective effort that transformed the depth, scope, and quality of their discussion.
eng114-14.ex:
句意：一整個早上，這種創新的討論過程＿＿＿一種新形式的集體合作，改變了討論的深度、範圍與品質。

討論過程「產生」新的合作形式 → (C) gave rise to ✓

(A) made up for 彌補（全國 34% 誤選；前文沒有需要彌補的損失）(B) kept track of 記錄、追蹤 (D) looked out for 留意、照顧。
eng114-14.k: give rise to＝導致、產生；討論方式「產生」了新形式的集體合作。

eng114-15.stem: Over the course of the morning, the innovative discussion process 14 a new form of collective effort that transformed the depth, scope, and quality of their discussion. The World Café was 15 created.
eng114-15.ex:
句意：世界咖啡館＿＿＿誕生了。

前一段說明雨天換桌討論的過程與結果 → 這一句是結果 → (D) thus 因此、就這樣 ✓

(A) still 仍然（全國 19% 誤選）(B) also 也 (C) further 進一步，都沒有「因此」的意思。
eng114-15.k: 前面描述了整個過程 → The World Café was thus created.＝世界咖啡館就這樣誕生了。

eng114-16.stem: It can 16 suddenly, progressing from a feeling of uneasiness to a cold sweat.
eng114-16.ex:
句意：暈動症可能突然＿＿＿，從一陣不舒服發展到冒冷汗。

疾病突然「發作、來襲」→ (D) strike ✓

(C) burst 爆裂、衝出（全國 44% 誤選；常見用法是 burst into tears、pipes burst，不用來說疾病發作）(A) crash 撞毀、當機 (B) flush 臉紅、沖水。
eng114-16.k: 疾病、災害突然「發作、侵襲」用 strike：motion sickness can strike suddenly。

eng114-17.stem: Motion sickness occurs when the signals your brain receives from your eyes, ears, and body 17 .
eng114-17.ex:
句意：當大腦從眼睛、耳朵和身體接收到的訊號＿＿＿時，就會產生暈動症。

下一句說這些部位 send conflicting information（傳送互相衝突的訊息）→ (C) do not match 不一致 ✓

(A) are not regular 不規律 (B) can hardly move 幾乎無法移動 (D) are rarely cued 很少被提示，都沒有「衝突」的意思。
eng114-17.k: 眼睛、耳朵、身體傳給大腦的訊號「不一致」就會暈。

eng114-18.stem: Your brain doesn’t know whether you are stationary or moving when these parts send conflicting information: One part of your balance-sensing system detects that your body is moving, but the other parts 18 .
eng114-18.ex:
句意：平衡感系統的一部分偵測到身體在動，但其他部分卻＿＿＿。

省略的是前面的一般動詞 detects（that…）→ 否定代動詞用 do／does；主詞 the other parts 是複數 → (C) don't ✓

(A) aren't（全國 43% 誤選）：把 is moving 當成要省略的部分，但這裡對比的是「有沒有偵測到」，不是「身體有沒有在動」。

(B) won't 未來式 (D) haven't 完成式，時態也不合。
eng114-18.k: but the other parts don't＝代動詞，代替前面的 detect that your body is moving。

eng114-19.stem: You can take some 19 to help avoid the discomfort.
eng114-19.ex:
句意：你可以採取一些＿＿＿來避免不舒服。

後面列出前排座位、看遠方、事先吃藥等方法，都是事先「預防」→ (B) preventive measures 預防措施 ✓（take measures 是固定搭配）

(A) special opportunities 特別的機會 (C) potential risks 潛在風險 (D) significant advantages 顯著的優點。
eng114-19.k: take measures＝採取措施；後面列出的方法都是「預防」。

eng114-20.stem: Looking out into the distance from the vehicle can help 20 .
eng114-20.ex:
句意：坐前排可以減少晃動；從車上看向遠方＿＿＿有幫助。

前一句已經提出一個方法，這句再補充另一個 → (A) as well 也 ✓

(B) by far 遠遠地（修飾最高級）(C) at least 至少 (D) after all 畢竟。
eng114-20.k: 前一句已經給了一個方法 → 看遠方「也」有幫助：help as well。

eng114-21.stem: Located at the heart of Paris, this medieval cathedral is 21 for its intricate architecture, stunning stained glass windows, and, above all, its bells.
eng114-21.ex:
句意：這座位在巴黎市中心的中世紀大教堂，以精細的建築、美麗的彩繪玻璃窗，尤其是它的鐘＿＿＿。

is ＿＿ for… → 需要形容詞或過去分詞；「以…聞名」是 be noted for → (I) noted ✓

(C) familiar（全國 20% 誤選）後面接 to／with，不接 for，而且第 26 題才用得到。

eng114-22.stem: In fact, there is documented 22 to the ringing of bells even before the cathedral’s construction was completed, dating as far back as the 12th century.
eng114-22.ex:
句意：事實上，早在大教堂完工以前（可追溯到 12 世紀），就有文獻＿＿＿敲鐘的事。

documented（有記載的）後面接名詞，名詞後面接 to → reference to（提到…）→ (A) reference ✓

eng114-23.stem: In fact, there is documented 22 to the ringing of bells even before the cathedral’s construction was completed, dating as far back as the 12th century. The 10 bells vary in size, each 23 a name.
eng114-23.ex:
句意：這 10 口鐘大小不一，每一口都＿＿＿一個名字。下一句就說最大的一口叫 Emmanuel。

each＋V-ing 是分詞構句（＝each of which bears a name）→ 需要 V-ing → (B) bearing 帶有 ✓

(I) noted（全國 30% 誤選）是過去分詞，「每一口都被注意到一個名字」不通。
eng114-23.k: each bearing a name＝每一口鐘都有一個名字（bear＝帶有）。

eng114-24.stem: It is the only one of the whole group that 24 the French Revolution, while the rest were melted down for weapons.
eng114-24.ex:
句意：它是整組鐘裡唯一＿＿＿法國大革命的一口，其他的都被熔掉做成武器。

that 後面需要動詞（過去式）；「其他都被熔掉」→ 它「倖存」→ (F) survived ✓
eng114-24.k: the only one that survived the French Revolution＝唯一在法國大革命中倖存的一口。

eng114-25.stem: But due to their poor acoustic quality, all of the bells were replaced in 2013—except for Emmanuel, which 25 its renowned, excellent sound.
eng114-25.ex:
句意：因為音質不好，2013 年所有的鐘都被換掉，只有 Emmanuel 例外，因為它＿＿＿了著名、優美的音色。

which 後面需要過去式動詞；其他鐘被換掉是因為音質差 → Emmanuel「保有」好音色 → (D) retained ✓
eng114-25.k: except for Emmanuel, which retained its sound＝只有 Emmanuel 保有著名的好音色。

eng114-26.stem: Over centuries, the bells have become a 26 part of life in Paris, where they are known as “the cathedral’s voice.”
eng114-26.ex:
句意：幾個世紀以來，這些鐘已成為巴黎生活中＿＿＿的一部分，被稱為「大教堂的聲音」。

a＋形容詞＋part → (C) familiar 熟悉的 ✓

(E) faithful（全國 24% 誤選）是「忠實的」，a faithful part of life 不通；faithful 要用在第 27 題。
eng114-26.k: a familiar part of life＝生活中熟悉的一部分。

eng114-27.stem: They have been used to mark the hours of the day, to call the 27 to prayer, and to signal emergency situations such as fires and invasions.
eng114-27.ex:
句意：這些鐘被用來報時、召喚＿＿＿來禱告，以及在火災、入侵等緊急情況時示警。

the＋形容詞可以表示「一群人」（例如 the rich 有錢人）；被召喚去禱告的是 the faithful（信徒）→ (E) ✓

這題全國答對率只有 26%，the＋形容詞＝一群人的用法要記住。
eng114-27.k: the faithful＝信徒（the＋形容詞＝一群人）；call the faithful to prayer＝召喚信徒禱告。

eng114-28.stem: They have also rung in times of 28 and of mourning, announcing such events as royal weddings and coronations of kings, as well as funerals of heads of state.
eng114-28.ex:
句意：這些鐘也在＿＿＿和哀悼的時刻響起，宣告王室婚禮、國王加冕，以及國家元首的喪禮。

and 對等連接 of mourning（哀悼）；婚禮、加冕是「慶祝」→ (G) celebration ✓

(B) bearing（全國 25% 誤選）放在 of 後面意思不通。
eng114-28.k: in times of celebration and of mourning＝在歡慶與哀悼的時刻。

eng114-29.stem: However, after the devastating fire that damaged the cathedral in 2019, the bells fell 29 .
eng114-29.ex:
句意：然而，2019 年那場嚴重的大火損壞了大教堂之後，鐘聲就＿＿＿了。

fall＋形容詞＝變成某種狀態（fall asleep 睡著、fall ill 生病）→ fell silent 沉寂下來 → (J) silent ✓
eng114-29.k: fall silent＝安靜下來、停止發聲（fall＋形容詞＝變成某種狀態）。

eng114-30.stem: The building went through a complex and time-consuming process of 30 , and the famous monument was finally reopened on December 8, 2024.
eng114-30.ex:
句意：這棟建築經過複雜又耗時的＿＿＿過程，終於在 2024 年 12 月 8 日重新開放。

of 後面接名詞；火災後重新開放 → 「修復」→ (H) restoration ✓
eng114-30.k: a process of restoration＝修復的過程。

eng114-31.stem:
Originated in Japan, these hotels were initially meant for business professionals to stay close to populated business districts without spending a lot. 31
空格 31 應填入哪一句？
o: In response to rising demands, these hotels are embracing a wave of innovation.
The room’s thin plastic walls easily transmit the sound of snoring made by neighboring guests.
The chambers are stacked side-by-side, two units high, with the upper rooms reached by a ladder.
Today, they provide low-budget, overnight lodging in commerce centers in large cities worldwide.
eng114-31.ex:
空格在第一段最後。前句：膠囊旅館起源於日本，原本是讓商務人士不必花大錢就能住在商業區附近。

接下來交代「現在」的狀況 → (D) Today, they provide low-budget, overnight lodging in commerce centers in large cities worldwide.（今天，它們在全球大城市的商業中心提供平價的過夜住宿）✓

Today 和前句的 initially（最初）形成對比。(A)「因應需求而創新」要到第三段講新型膠囊旅館時才出現（全國 24% 誤選）。
eng114-31.k: 第一段先說起源與最初的用途，空格接著說「今天」的情況 → Today, they provide… worldwide.

eng114-32.stem:
The walls of each capsule may be made of wood, metal or any rigid material, but are often fiberglass or plastic. 32 Each capsule is equipped with a comfortable mattress, a small light, and sometimes a television or other entertainment options. Such minimalist design is what makes these hotels both inexpensive and efficient, providing only the essential elements for a good night sleep.
空格 32 應填入哪一句？
o: In response to rising demands, these hotels are embracing a wave of innovation.
The room’s thin plastic walls easily transmit the sound of snoring made by neighboring guests.
The chambers are stacked side-by-side, two units high, with the upper rooms reached by a ladder.
Today, they provide low-budget, overnight lodging in commerce centers in large cities worldwide.
eng114-32.ex:
第二段在描述膠囊房間：大約一張單人床大、牆壁的材質；空格後說每個膠囊有床墊、小燈、電視。

空格也是房間外觀與配置的描述 → (C) The chambers are stacked side-by-side, two units high, with the upper rooms reached by a ladder.（膠囊並排堆疊成兩層，上層用梯子進入）✓

(B) 講塑膠牆隔音差、會聽到隔壁打呼，是「缺點」，屬於最後一段（全國 43% 誤選）。
eng114-32.k: 第二段描述房間：大小、牆壁材質 → 接著描述膠囊如何堆疊（兩層、用梯子上去）。

eng114-33.stem:
Pod hotels are also seen in Europe and North America, especially in big cities like New York, London, and Paris. 33 Instead of the traditional bare pod-sized style, new chains now feature interior design that appeals to digitally connected travelers from around the world. Guests may enjoy facilities such as free Wi-Fi, mobile charging, and even a soundless alarm system that raises the sleeping guests into a seated position while gradually brightening the lights.
空格 33 應填入哪一句？
o: In response to rising demands, these hotels are embracing a wave of innovation.
The room’s thin plastic walls easily transmit the sound of snoring made by neighboring guests.
The chambers are stacked side-by-side, two units high, with the upper rooms reached by a ladder.
Today, they provide low-budget, overnight lodging in commerce centers in large cities worldwide.
eng114-33.ex:
前句：膠囊旅館已擴展到歐洲與北美的大城市。空格後：新的連鎖店不再是傳統簡陋的樣式，改用吸引數位旅客的室內設計，還有免費 Wi-Fi 等設施。

空格要帶出「改變」→ (A) In response to rising demands, these hotels are embracing a wave of innovation.（為了因應日益增加的需求，這些旅館掀起一波創新）✓

innovation 對應後面的 new chains、interior design。(D) Today… 是總覽句，應放在第一段（全國 24% 誤選）。
eng114-33.k: 空格後說新連鎖店改用吸引數位旅客的設計 → 空格先說「因應需求開始創新」。

eng114-34.stem:
Some hotels may not provide air conditioning in the capsules, leading to poor air flow. 34 Also, you may have to share common facilities (such as bathrooms) with other guests. And, if you’re worried about feeling claustrophobic in small spaces, you’d better think twice before making a reservation.
空格 34 應填入哪一句？
o: In response to rising demands, these hotels are embracing a wave of innovation.
The room’s thin plastic walls easily transmit the sound of snoring made by neighboring guests.
The chambers are stacked side-by-side, two units high, with the upper rooms reached by a ladder.
Today, they provide low-budget, overnight lodging in commerce centers in large cities worldwide.
eng114-34.ex:
最後一段說膠囊旅館不一定適合每個人，依序列出缺點：沒有冷氣、通風差；空格；Also（此外）要和別人共用浴室；如果怕狹小空間最好三思。

空格也是一個缺點 → (B) The room's thin plastic walls easily transmit the sound of snoring made by neighboring guests.（薄薄的塑膠牆很容易傳來隔壁房客的打呼聲）✓

thin plastic walls 呼應第二段說牆壁常用塑膠做。(C) 描述房間的配置，屬於第二段（全國 27% 誤選）。
eng114-34.k: 最後一段列缺點：通風差 → 牆薄會聽到打呼 → 要共用浴室 → 怕狹小空間要三思。

o: The inventors of traffic lights in history.
eng114-35.ex:
第 1–2 段：Knight 把鐵路號誌改成交通號誌（1868 年）；第 3 段：美國的改良與黃燈（1920 年）；第 4 段：有了自駕車，也許不再需要號誌。

全文重點是交通管制方式如何一路演變 → (A) The evolution of traffic control systems. ✓

(B) 發明者（Knight、Potts）只是各階段的例子，第 4 段的自駕車管理就和發明者無關（全國 43% 誤選）。
eng114-35.k: 全文依時間寫交通號誌的演變：鐵路臂式號誌 → 美國的紅綠燈與黃燈 → 自駕車時代可能不需要號誌。

eng114-36.ex:
第 1 段：Knight 依照鐵路的可動臂號誌設計，手臂水平伸出表示停止、放低到 45 度表示通行，並加上紅、綠煤氣燈供夜間使用。

圖中同時有兩支可動手臂和燈的是 (C) ✓

(A) 是只有燈、沒有手臂的號誌塔（全國 35% 誤選）(B) 只有手臂、沒有燈 (D) 是寫著 STOP／GO 的燈箱。
eng114-36.k: Knight 的號誌＝鐵路的「可動手臂」＋夜間用的紅綠煤氣燈 → 同時有手臂和燈的 (C)。

eng114-37.stem: Which of the following statements is true, according to the passage?
o: Knight was injured in the explosion of his traffic light.
Potts’ traffic light was the first one to appear in the USA.
The first traffic signal originated from the idea of a traffic director.
Future vehicles may not need traffic lights to cross an intersection.
eng114-37.ex:
第 4 段：研究者認為有了自駕車，交通號誌可能不再必要，車子會自動調整速度通過路口 → (D) ✓

(A) 在爆炸中受傷的是操作號誌的警察，不是 Knight。

(B) Potts 發明的是加上黃燈的三色號誌；在那之前，美國大城市已經有英國號誌的改良版。

(C) 號誌源自鐵路的可動臂號誌，只是手勢「像」交通指揮員，不是來自指揮員的想法（全國 21% 誤選）。
eng114-37.k: 最後一段：自駕車會自動調整速度通過路口，號誌可能不再需要。

eng114-38.stem: Here is a sentence: “This design was adopted in later traffic light designs across the world.” Which paragraph is most suitable to have it as the final sentence?
eng114-38.ex:
句子：This design was adopted in later traffic light designs across the world.（這個設計後來被世界各地的號誌沿用）

This design 要接在描述一個設計的句子後面；第 3 段最後正好在介紹 Potts 的三色號誌（加上「小心前進」的黃燈），而今天全世界都有黃燈 → (C) Paragraph 3 ✓

第 2 段最後是號誌被禁用，第 4 段講未來可能不需要號誌，接這句都不合理。
eng114-38.k: 「這個設計後來被全世界沿用」→ 放在介紹 Potts 三色號誌（黃燈）的第 3 段最後。

eng114-39.stem: What field of study does the research mentioned in the passage most likely belong to?
eng114-39.ex:
文中的研究內容：safe fear（安全的恐懼）、釋放壓抑的情緒、焦慮、創傷、睡眠、對暴力的敏感度，都在談人的心理與行為 → (A) Psychology 心理學 ✓

(B) Education 教育 (C) Philosophy 哲學 (D) Communication 傳播，都不是這些研究的主題。
eng114-39.k: 研究談的是恐怖片對情緒、焦慮、創傷、睡眠與行為的影響 → 心理學。

eng114-40.stem: What does the author mean by “learning vicariously” in the second paragraph?
eng114-40.ex:
原文：觀眾被故事吸引，會站在角色的角度、不自覺地預演劇情；研究者認為觀眾用這種方式 learning vicariously，學到面對真實威脅的技巧。

觀眾沒有親身經歷，而是透過「觀看」角色來學 → (B) Gaining knowledge through observation.（透過觀察獲得知識）✓

(D) 從「親身經驗」獲得資訊，意思正好相反（全國 25% 誤選）(C) 面對面互動 (A) 毫無保留地提問。
eng114-40.k: vicariously＝間接地、透過別人的經驗；觀眾「看」角色的遭遇來學習。

eng114-41.stem: Which of the following statements about horror movies can be inferred from the passage?
o: Most horror movie lovers are prone to aggressive behavior.
There are far more benefits to horror movies than disadvantages.
COVID-19 was an important source of inspiration for horror movies.
Watching horror movies may have a long-term effect on personality.
eng114-41.ex:
第 3 段最後：14 歲以下看恐怖片的孩子，成年後比較容易焦慮；接觸血腥暴力會讓他們對真實暴力比較不敏感、比較能接受攻擊行為。

這些都是長期的影響 → 可以推論 (D) Watching horror movies may have a long-term effect on personality. ✓

(A) 文中只說可能對「兒童」有負面影響，沒有說大多數愛看恐怖片的人有攻擊傾向。

(B) 文章好處、壞處都談，沒有比較哪一邊比較多。

(C) 疫情期間恐怖片觀看量高，不是「疫情啟發了恐怖片」（全國 19% 誤選）。
eng114-41.k: 最後一段：14 歲以下看恐怖片，成年後較容易焦慮，也可能對暴力變得麻木 → 可能有長期影響。

eng114-42.stem: How does the author develop the ideas in this passage?
o: By showing opposing views of an issue.
By presenting cause and effect of a problem.
By providing steps for settling a disagreement.
eng114-42.ex:
第 1 段：有人覺得恐怖片太可怕、有人愛看，研究開始釐清它的好處與風險；第 2 段（One benefit…）談好處；第 3 段（However…）談壞處。

作者用「正反兩面」來發展全文 → (B) By showing opposing views of an issue. ✓

(C) 呈現問題的因果（全國 38% 誤選）：文中雖然提到看恐怖片造成的影響，但全文架構是好處對照壞處，不是分析一個問題的原因和結果。

(A) 定義並舉例說明一個概念（safe fear 只是第 2 段的一小部分）(D) 提供解決爭議的步驟。
eng114-42.k: 第 2 段談恐怖片的好處、第 3 段談壞處 → 呈現一個議題的正反兩面。

eng115-01.stem: The mayor has such a ＿＿＿＿ schedule that it takes weeks to arrange an interview with her.
eng115-01.ex:
句意：市長的行程非常＿＿＿，要安排一次訪談得等好幾週。

(B) tight 緊湊的 ✓——tight schedule 是固定搭配。

(A) hasty 倉促的（形容動作或決定）(C) diligent 勤勉的（形容人）(D) routine 例行的，都無法說明「要等好幾週」。

eng115-02.stem: Jane started as an ＿＿＿＿ art designer, but now she has a professional studio of her own.
eng115-02.ex:
句意：Jane 一開始是＿＿＿的美術設計師，但現在已經有自己的專業工作室。

but 前後對比：一開始「業餘」→ 現在「專業」→ (C) amateur ✓

(D) elementary 是「初級的、基本的」（elementary school），不是「業餘」，全國 23% 誤選。

(A) official 官方的 (B) instant 立即的。
eng115-02.k: amateur 業餘的 ↔ professional 專業的，句中用 but 形成對比。

eng115-03.stem: The teaching ＿＿＿＿ at the famous high school soon attracted more than a dozen well-qualified applicants.
eng115-03.ex:
句意：這所名校的教職＿＿＿很快吸引了十多位條件優秀的應徵者。

有「應徵者」→ 需要的是「職缺」→ (B) vacancy ✓

(A) career 職業生涯 (C) expectation 期待 (D) inspiration 靈感。
eng115-03.k: teaching vacancy＝教職缺額，才會吸引應徵者（applicants）。

eng115-04.stem: Designed by a young engineer, the new product has created far more profit than ＿＿＿＿ expected.
eng115-04.ex:
句意：這項由年輕工程師設計的新產品，創造的利潤遠超過＿＿＿預期。

(A) initially 起初、原本 ✓——than initially expected 是常見說法。

(B) genuinely 真誠地 (C) alternatively 或者 (D) fundamentally 根本上。
eng115-04.k: than initially expected＝比原本預期的還要多。

eng115-05.stem: It has been confirmed that a balanced ＿＿＿＿ of fruit and vegetables is a key element to good health.
eng115-05.ex:
句意：已證實均衡＿＿＿蔬果是健康的關鍵。

(D) consumption 攝取、食用 ✓

(A) dimension 維度 (B) integration 整合 (C) provision 供應（是「提供」，不是「吃」）。
eng115-05.k: a balanced consumption of fruit and vegetables＝均衡攝取蔬果。

eng115-06.stem: As a shy boy afraid of making public appearances, Timmy ＿＿＿＿ the thought of speaking before large audiences.
eng115-06.ex:
句意：Timmy 是個害羞、怕公開露面的男孩，他＿＿＿在一大群人面前說話的念頭。

前面說他 afraid of making public appearances → (A) dreads 懼怕 ✓

(B) stresses 強調（全國 30% 誤選）(C) wanders 漫遊 (D) escapes 逃脫。

這題 A、B、D 選擇率接近，代表 dread 是很多人不熟的高頻字。

eng115-07.stem: To the newly-crowned winner of the piano competition, music is his life’s ＿＿＿＿ , which he has devoted himself to whole-heartedly.
eng115-07.ex:
句意：對這位剛奪冠的鋼琴家來說，音樂是他一生的＿＿＿，他全心投入其中。

(C) passion 熱情 ✓

(A) resource 資源 (B) impact 影響 (D) emphasis 強調。
eng115-07.k: life's passion＝一生的熱情所在，呼應 devoted himself to（全心投入）。

eng115-08.stem: The drunk driver who shouted at passers-by and ＿＿＿＿ them with glass bottles was quickly arrested by the police.

eng114-g11.html:
In 1995, a group of business and academic leaders met at the home of Juanita Brown and David Isaacs in Mill Valley, California. None of them had any idea they were about to create a social innovation that 11 rapidly around the world.

The group was supposed to have a large-circle discussion in their beautiful garden. Unfortunately, it started pouring. With their plan 12 by the rain, the two dozen participants squeezed into the living room. They broke into small, intimate table conversations, recording their insights on paper tablecloths. They periodically stopped their conversations to switch tables so the insights and ideas might 13 and deepen. As they moved from one table to another, they noticed new ideas emerging from the discussions. This in turn enriched subsequent rounds of conversation. Over the course of the morning, the innovative discussion process 14 a new form of collective effort that transformed the depth, scope, and quality of their discussion.

The World Café was 15 created. Since that rainy morning in Mill Valley, the World Café approach has been applied to multi-group discussions and cooperative actions by businesses, industries, and educational institutions around the world.

eng114-g16.html:
If you have ever been sick to your stomach on a rocking boat or a bumpy car ride, you know the discomfort of motion sickness. It can 16 suddenly, progressing from a feeling of uneasiness to a cold sweat. Soon, it can lead to dizziness, nausea, and vomiting.

Motion sickness occurs when the signals your brain receives from your eyes, ears, and body 17 . Your brain doesn’t know whether you are stationary or moving when these parts send conflicting information: One part of your balance-sensing system detects that your body is moving, but the other parts 18 . Your brain’s confused reaction makes you feel sick. You may experience the discomfort from the motion of cars, boats, or amusement park rides. You may also get sick from playing video games, or looking through a microscope.

You can take some 19 to help avoid the discomfort. If you are traveling, reserve seats where motion is felt the least, such as the front row of a car or forward cars of a train. Looking out into the distance from the vehicle can help 20 . You can also take medicine before your ride to avoid or reduce nausea and vomiting.

eng114-g21.html:
The Notre-Dame de Paris is one of the most famous cathedrals in Europe. Located at the heart of Paris, this medieval cathedral is 21 for its intricate architecture, stunning stained glass windows, and, above all, its bells.

Mounted in the two tall towers of the cathedral, Notre-Dame’s bells have been ringing for over 800 years. In fact, there is documented 22 to the ringing of bells even before the cathedral’s construction was completed, dating as far back as the 12th century. The 10 bells vary in size, each 23 a name. The largest one, named “Emmanuel,” weighs over 13 tons. It is the only one of the whole group that 24 the French Revolution, while the rest were melted down for weapons. The melted bells were recast in the late 19th century. But due to their poor acoustic quality, all of the bells were replaced in 2013—except for Emmanuel, which 25 its renowned, excellent sound. This particular bell, ringing in F sharp, is considered one of the most harmonically beautiful in Europe.

Over centuries, the bells have become a 26 part of life in Paris, where they are known as “the cathedral’s voice.” They have been used to mark the hours of the day, to call the 27 to prayer, and to signal emergency situations such as fires and invasions. They have also rung in times of 28 and of mourning, announcing such events as royal weddings and coronations of kings, as well as funerals of heads of state.

However, after the devastating fire that damaged the cathedral in 2019, the bells fell 29 . The building went through a complex and time-consuming process of 30 , and the famous monument was finally reopened on December 8, 2024. The sounds of Notre-Dame bells once again filled the air in Paris, and will be heard for generations to come.

eng114-g31.html:
A capsule hotel, also known as a pod hotel, is a unique type of basic, affordable accommodation. Originated in Japan, these hotels were initially meant for business professionals to stay close to populated business districts without spending a lot. 31

A typical room of a capsule hotel is roughly the length and width of a single bed, with sufficient height for a guest to crawl in and sit up on the bed. The walls of each capsule may be made of wood, metal or any rigid material, but are often fiberglass or plastic. 32 Each capsule is equipped with a comfortable mattress, a small light, and sometimes a television or other entertainment options. Such minimalist design is what makes these hotels both inexpensive and efficient, providing only the essential elements for a good night sleep.

The first capsule hotel, the Capsule Inn Osaka, opened in 1979. Since then, capsule hotels have quickly spread to other cities and countries. Chains have emerged in Taiwan, Singapore, and even on resort islands like Bali. Pod hotels are also seen in Europe and North America, especially in big cities like New York, London, and Paris. 33 Instead of the traditional bare pod-sized style, new chains now feature interior design that appeals to digitally connected travelers from around the world. Guests may enjoy facilities such as free Wi-Fi, mobile charging, and even a soundless alarm system that raises the sleeping guests into a seated position while gradually brightening the lights.

While offering budget-conscious travelers a unique option, capsule hotels may not be suitable for everyone. Some hotels may not provide air conditioning in the capsules, leading to poor air flow. 34 Also, you may have to share common facilities (such as bathrooms) with other guests. And, if you’re worried about feeling claustrophobic in small spaces, you’d better think twice before making a reservation.

eng114-g35.html:
While waiting to cross the street at busy intersections, have you ever wondered who invented the traffic light? Most people credit the first traffic light to Nottingham engineer John Peake Knight. A railway manager, Knight specialized in designing the signaling system for Britain’s growing railway network in the 1860s. He saw no reason why this could not be adapted for use on the busy London intersections. Thus, he proposed a signaling system based on the railway movable-arm signal: Arms extending horizontally commanded drivers to stop, whereas arms lowered to a 45-degree angle told drivers to move on, resembling a traffic director’s gestures. Red and green gas lamps were added to the signal for use at night. A police officer was stationed by the side to operate the system.

Knight’s traffic signal was installed near London’s Westminster Bridge in December 1868, but the system was short-lived. A gas leak one month later caused an explosion in the lights, injuring the policeman operating it. Deemed a public hazard, the project was immediately dropped, and traffic lights were banned until their return in 1929 back to the British streets.

In the early 1900s, versions of the British traffic lights appeared in big cities in America, where traffic was on a sharp rise. Systems using movable arms were popular in Chicago, while those using the red and green lights were adopted in San Francisco. Patents with innovations on Knight’s ideas were filed nationwide. A major breakthrough was the yellow light invented by a Detroit police officer William Potts. Installed in Detroit in 1920, Potts’ three-color system allowed for the added signal “proceed with caution” to be displayed.

Now, with the emergence of self-driving cars, researchers have begun to suggest that traffic signals are no longer necessary. Intersections will operate in a way that cars automatically adjust their speed to cross through, while maintaining safe distances from other vehicles. In the near future, we may experience a brand new form of traffic management!

eng114-g39.html:
Typically featuring zombies and serial killers, horror movies are too frightening to be fun for some people. But many others enjoy a good fear spectacle, and line up to see the latest scary movie. Given the variations in preferences, new studies have started to untangle the benefits and risks of horror movies.

One benefit of horror movies revolves around the concept of so-called “safe fear.” When watching a frightening film, people are in the comfort of their own home or theater seats rather than under the threat of any real danger. In a controlled environment, these films may actually reduce the negative impact on viewers and help them become tougher. Secondly, as people are drawn into the story, they tend to take the perspective of the characters and rehearse the plot unconsciously. Researchers believe that viewers are learning vicariously this way, picking up tips on how to handle threats in the real world. In addition, studies show that the thrill and excitement linked with scary films can be therapeutic: It allows viewers to release bottled-up emotions and experience a sense of relief after the movie is over. This probably explains why during the COVID-19 pandemic, horror and pandemic thrillers were the most-watched movies on digital movie apps.

However, researchers also find that horror movies can have negative effects on some people. People who are more sensitive to anxiety can panic after viewing a thriller. For those with unpleasant experiences, trauma may be triggered by the themes and images in the movies, which could make their symptoms worse. Furthermore, watching horror movies can disturb sleep patterns, as the residual fear and anxiety they evoke may keep people awake all night, thus leading to fatigue and irritability the following day. Finally, specialists warn that frightening films can have a negative impact on children. Children under 14 who watch horror movies have a greater chance of developing anxiety later in adulthood. Worse yet, exposure to graphic violence and bloodshed can make them less sensitive to real-life violence and more accepting of aggression.
